name: Leipzig/Halle Airport
before:
One airport for two cities, at Schkeuditz between Leipzig in Saxony and Halle in Saxony-Anhalt. For passengers it is Germany's twelfth largest, with more than 2.19 million in 2024, mostly on European leisure routes.

Freight is the real story. It is DHL Aviation's main European hub and AeroLogic's home base, open around the clock for cargo, and it records more freight-only movements than any other airport in the European Union. In 2024 it handled 1,383,319 tonnes, second in Germany behind Frankfurt and fourth in Europe.

The layout is kind to a tired client. The terminal is compact with short walking distances, the main car park is built into it, and a pier of six jet bridges runs off it. Note that there is immigration for international arrivals but no international transfer area.

The railway station sits directly beneath the terminal, with Intercity trains on the Dresden to Cologne route and two S-Bahn lines into Leipzig and Halle.
after:
One airport for two cities, at Schkeuditz between Leipzig in Saxony and Halle in Saxony-Anhalt. For passengers it is Germany's fifteenth largest, with about 2.1 million in 2025, mostly on leisure routes.

Freight is the real story. It is AeroLogic's home base and is open around the clock for cargo flights. In 2025 it handled about 1.39 million tonnes of cargo, second in Germany behind Frankfurt.

The railway station sits directly beneath the terminal, with two S-Bahn lines into Leipzig and Halle.

claims.claim: Germany's fifteenth largest for passengers, about 2.1 million in 2025
claims.inAfter: For passengers it is Germany's fifteenth largest, with about 2.1 million in 2025
claims.note: Was 'twelfth largest, with more than 2.19 million in 2024'. A passenger total replaces a passenger total. ADV's full-year 2025 table has 2,119,170 (down 3.7%) and Eurostat 2,111,512; both rank it fifteenth, behind Frankfurt, Munich, Berlin, Dusseldorf, Hamburg, Cologne Bonn, Stuttgart, Hanover, Nuremberg, Memmingen, Dortmund, Karlsruhe/Baden-Baden, Weeze (Niederrhein) and Hahn, and ahead of Bremen. It fell from twelfth as Karlsruhe, Weeze and Hahn grew.

claims.note: Was 'mostly on European leisure routes'. Eurostat's route figures (2024, the latest it publishes by route) put about three quarters of the passengers on holiday routes: Antalya, Hurghada, Palma, Heraklion, the Canaries, Rhodes, Marsa Alam, Corfu, Kos, Varna, Burgas and Madeira carried 1,557,193 of the 2,040,517 on the routes listed. 'European' is dropped because Hurghada and Marsa Alam are in Egypt. The airport's live board tonight still shows Corendon from Hurghada, Marabu from Mallorca and Freebird from Heraklion.
